prompt: Count the ways to climb n stairs taking 1, 2, or 3 at a time -- with a Map memo, so a 60-stair staircase finishes instantly instead of taking hours. Complete both countWays overloads, then run the tests.
explanation: Naive triple recursion re-solves the same staircase heights exponentially many times; memoisation turns that into linear work by remembering each answer the first time it is computed. The shape is always the same three steps: look the argument up in the map and return early on a hit, compute the value otherwise, then put it in the map before returning. The one-argument overload exists purely to hide the bookkeeping map from callers, and long is needed because the counts outgrow int well before n reaches 60.
hints: Order matters: check memo.containsKey(n) BEFORE doing any work, and memo.put(n, ways) just before you return.
Handle n < 0 by returning 0 without storing anything, then the base cases 0, 1 and 2, then the three recursive calls.
The one-argument overload is a single line -- return countWays(n, new HashMap<>()) -- and every value must be a long, not an int.
